newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on weather and soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on weather and soybeans.

text.p: Renewed concerns about harsh weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region and a rally in soybeans boosted CBOT wheat futures to higher closes, traders said.
Support also came from ideas more rain is needed in dry European areas to stem further deterioration of wheat there.
"They're going to get some rain in Europe but they need a lot more and there's a lot of rain in the Panhandle of Texas and in Oklahoma," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Meteorologists forecast a return to dryness soon in France.

Light to moderate rain now developing over parched areas of England and France should increase into the weekend, but beyond that, weather could turn drier and warmer, independent U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said Friday.
It's dry in Europe but portions of the U.S. are too wet.
Forecasters expect up to a foot of snow in the Texas Panhandle which could further damage wheat hurt there by a freeze nearly two weeks ago, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Wheat closed unchanged to nine cents per bushel higher, with July up 6-1/2 at $4.32-1/4.
"Now they're talking rains in the Plains. The talk of five inch rains may not be good (for the crop)," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Traders also said the market remains on edge amid the recent variety of damage estimates released following the freeze in the U.S. Great Plains on April 12-13.

Wheat tumbled late Thursday on talk that key U.S. Midwest cooperative Farmland Industries pegged the freeze loss in hard red winter wheat at not more than 117 million bushels. There have been estimates from other industry watchers that up to 290 million bushels have been lost.

A Farmland statement Friday declined to acknowledge the damage estimates and a Farmland official said the co-op believes that high estimates that have circulated through the industry of the damaged crop were overstated.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 33,580 traded Thursday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures sold 400 July $4.70 calls at 12 cents, sold 400 July $4.20 puts at 16-1/2 cents, sold 200 July $4.80 calls at nine cents and sold 200 July $4.10 puts at 14 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 13,397 traded Thursday.
